title: Global derived Hom adjunction
statement: Let X and Y be quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, and let f:X\to Y be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Let Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image] have its right adjoint a, whose existence is supplied by [lem-pc-qcqs-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint]. For P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X) and K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(Y), there is a natural isomorphism of global derived Hom complexes $$R\operatorname{Hom}_X(P,a(K))\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*P,K)$$ [def-pc-global-derived-rhom].

source.place: Tag 0AA8 (Lemma 48.6.2), global Hom adjunction in case (1)

proof.text: The qcqs hypotheses ensure that the restricted derived direct image preserves D_{\mathrm{QCoh}} and has right adjoint a, with counit (the sheafy trace) Rf_*a(K)\to K, by [lem-pc-qcqs-derived-direct-image-right-adjoint]. Use the counit-induced internal-Hom comparison stated in [lem-pc-qcqs-sheaf-rhom-adjunction]; that node records the canonical map and says that after applying the coherator DQ_Y it is an isomorphism. Its construction from the counit is natural in P and K.

Apply derived global sections to the comparison map of [lem-pc-qcqs-sheaf-rhom-adjunction]. Let p_X:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(\{\mathrm{pt}\},\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)) and p_Y:(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to(\{\mathrm{pt}\},\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)) be the morphisms of ringed spaces of [def-pc-global-derived-rhom], so R\Gamma(X,-)=Rp_{X,*} and R\Gamma(Y,-)=Rp_{Y,*}, and let r:(\{\mathrm{pt}\},\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X))\to(\{\mathrm{pt}\},\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)) be given by f^\sharp:\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X), so p_Y\circ f=r\circ p_X and Rr_*=r_* is the exact restriction of scalars. Applying the canonical composition isomorphism [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition] to both factorizations gives the derived Leray identity R\Gamma(Y,-)\circ Rf_*\cong r_*\circ R\Gamma(X,-) on D(\mathcal O_X). Thus [def-pc-global-derived-rhom] identifies the two sides with R\operatorname{Hom}_X(P,a(K)) (with scalars restricted to \Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)) and R\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_*P,K). Since the map becomes an isomorphism after DQ_Y, [lem-pc-dq-coherator-adjunction] (Y is quasi-compact and quasi-separated) gives a quasi-isomorphism on R\Gamma(Y,-): in each degree use H^i(Y,E)=Hom(\mathcal O_Y[-i],DQ_Y E), with \mathcal O_Y[-i] quasi-coherent. This also gives naturality in P and K.
